P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: No. There are no limits on inflows or outflows of funds apart from withholding taxes on certain payments. The riyal has been fixed by SAMA at 3.75 per USD since 1986.

sources.title: Saudi Arabia Country Commercial Guide — Trade Financing
sources.quote: Foreign Exchange Controls There is no limitation in Saudi Arabia on the inflow or outflow of funds for remittances of profits, debt service, capital, capital gains, returns on intellectual property, or imported inputs, other than certain withholding taxes

sources.title: Saudi Arabia Country Commercial Guide — Trade Financing
sources.quote: Since 1986, when the last currency devaluation occurred, the official exchange rate has been fixed by SAMA at 3.75 Saudi riyals per U.S.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. SAMA's rulebook (in force since 2019) lets customers open accounts in any available foreign currency and deposit and withdraw in it; if that currency is unavailable, payment can be made in Saudi riyals, and normal fees are borne by the customer (SAMA). The riyal is pegged to the US dollar (not captured here).

sources.title: Foreign Currency Accounts
sources.quote: Status: In-Force Customers may open accounts in any available foreign currency.

sources.title: Foreign Currency Accounts
sources.quote: If such foreign currency is not available, payments can be made in Saudi riyal.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Saudi nationals can get a Freelance Document/License from the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development via the official freelance platform. It is valid for one year, renewable, and covers 120+ specialties. Expatriates cannot use this route and generally need a commercial registration or a licensed company (sponsorship/investment rules apply).

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: Official TIN description supplied by Saudi Arabia to the OECD: "TIN is issued by the General Authority for Zakat and Tax (GAZT) to all taxpayers and withholding entities ( such as government ministries, agencies and departments). GAZT is the Saudi Arabian tax administration . TIN is issued once to a taxpayer; it remains valid as long as the taxpayer is in operation. The taxpayer's TIN is used for all the taxes to which the taxpayer is liable." How a freelancer applies (forms, online portal, fees) was not captured.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: There is no individual income tax scheme, and employment earnings are not taxed. Non-employment (business) income is taxed as an entity or PE: non-Saudi owners pay 20% income tax, while Saudi/GCC owners' share pays zakat (2.5% basis, not captured). Deloitte 2026 agrees: employment income is not taxed, but an individual's business income may face corporate income tax, withholding tax or zakat depending on nationality and residence.

sources.title: Saudi Arabia - Individual - Taxes on personal income
sources.quote: There is no individual income tax scheme in Saudi Arabia. Income tax is not imposed on an individual's earnings if they are derived only from employment in Saudi Arabia. Non-employment income is taxed as an entity or permanent establishment (PE).

sources.title: Saudi Arabia Highlights 2026
sources.quote: Individual taxation Individuals are not subject to income tax on employment income.

sources.title: Saudi Arabia Highlights 2026
sources.quote: However, individuals may be subject to corporate income tax, withholding tax, or zakat on business income depending on their nationality and residence.

L3_income_tax_foreign.notes: TRAP: freelance/business income of individuals is NOT simply tax-free - it falls under the entity rules (zakat for Saudis, 20% tax for non-Saudis).

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT is 15% (since 1 July 2020). Registration is mandatory above SAR 375,000 of taxable supplies in 12 months, and voluntary between SAR 187,500 and 375,000. Exports of goods and services and certain cross-border services consumed outside Saudi Arabia are zero-rated, with input VAT recoverable.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: The Personal Data Protection Law (Royal Decree M/19, amended by M/148) took effect on 14 September 2023, with compliance generally required by 14 September 2024. Implementing Regulations and Transfer Regulations are in force; SDAIA is the regulator. It applies across sectors and partly extraterritorially.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: The E-Commerce Law (in force October 2019) lets consumers return goods or terminate services bought online within 7 days of receipt if unused, subject to exceptions, and cancel if delivery is delayed more than 15 days. The consumer bears return costs unless agreed otherwise. Online sellers must register and disclose identity; the Ministry of Commerce enforces, with fines of up to SAR 1 million reported.

sources.title: Saudi Arabia implements its new E-Commerce Law
sources.quote: Furthermore, the E-Commerce Law includes a provision that consumers may return goods, or terminate a contract of service, obtained through an e-commerce channel, within seven days of receipt, if they have not used or benefitted from the goods or services - except for certain circumstances that are set out in the E-Commerce Law.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Send, receive, and withdraw'). (6) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
